subject: Biology
question: Assertion: White muscle fibres depend on anaerobic processes for energy. Reason: White muscle fibres contain a high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.

options.A: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

subject: Biology
question: The central neural system (CNS) of humans includes:

options.A: the brain and the cranial nerves
options.B: the brain and the visceral nerves
options.C: the spinal cord and the spinal nerves
options.D: the brain and the spinal cord

correct_answer: the brain and the spinal cord
explanation: The CNS includes the brain and the spinal cord and is the site of information processing and control. All nerves associated with the CNS form the PNS.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

subject: Biology
question: Afferent nerve fibres of the PNS transmit impulses:

options.B: from the CNS to skeletal muscles only
options.C: from tissues and organs to the CNS
options.D: from the CNS to peripheral tissues and organs

correct_answer: from tissues and organs to the CNS
explanation: Afferent fibres transmit impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS, while efferent fibres carry regulatory impulses from the CNS to peripheral tissues and organs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

subject: Biology
question: Fibres that transmit regulatory impulses from the CNS to the concerned peripheral tissues and organs are:
explanation: Efferent fibres carry regulatory impulses from the CNS to peripheral tissues and organs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

subject: Biology
question_type: Match List I and List II
question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Somatic neural system; (Q) Autonomic neural system; (R) Afferent fibres; (S) Visceral nervous system. List II: (I) Nerves, fibres, ganglia and plexuses linking the CNS and viscera; (II) Relays impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles; (III) Transmits impulses from the CNS to involuntary organs and smooth muscles; (IV) Carry impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS. Choose the correct option.
explanation: The somatic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles; the autonomic neural system to involuntary organs and smooth muscles; afferent fibres carry impulses to the CNS; the visceral nervous system is the complex of nerves, fibres, ganglia and plexuses linking the CNS and the viscera.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: The autonomic neural system transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles of the body. Reason: The autonomic neural system is a division of the central neural system.

options.A: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: the PNS is divided into the somatic and the autonomic neural systems, so the autonomic system is part of the PNS, not the CNS.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: The somatic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs of the body. Statement II: The PNS comprises all the nerves of the body associated with the CNS.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is incorrect: the somatic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles; involuntary organs are served by the autonomic system. Statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements about the visceral nervous system. I. It is a part of the peripheral neural system. II. It comprises the whole complex of nerves, fibres, ganglia and plexuses. III. It carries impulses only from the CNS to the viscera. IV. It also carries impulses from the viscera to the CNS. Which of these are correct?
explanation: The visceral nervous system is part of the PNS comprising nerves, fibres, ganglia and plexuses through which impulses travel from the CNS to the viscera and from the viscera to the CNS. Conduction is in both directions, so III is wrong.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

subject: Biology
question: In a flow chart of the human neural system, the boxes 'Sympathetic neural system' and 'Parasympathetic neural system' branch directly from the box labelled:
explanation: The PNS is divided into the somatic and the autonomic neural systems, and the autonomic system is further classified into the sympathetic and parasympathetic neural systems.

subject: Biology
question: All of the following belong to the peripheral neural system except:
explanation: The spinal cord, with the brain, forms the CNS. Afferent and efferent fibres and the somatic and autonomic systems belong to the PNS.

subject: Biology
question: A toxin blocks conduction only in efferent fibres of the PNS, leaving afferent fibres intact. Which outcome is expected?

options.A: Impulses from organs reach the CNS, but regulatory impulses fail to reach peripheral organs
options.B: Impulses in both directions fail, since both fibre types travel together
options.C: Impulses in both directions continue, as the CNS itself is unaffected
options.D: Impulses from organs fail to reach the CNS, but regulatory impulses reach peripheral organs

correct_answer: Impulses from organs reach the CNS, but regulatory impulses fail to reach peripheral organs
explanation: Afferent fibres carry impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS and remain working. Efferent fibres carry regulatory impulses from the CNS to peripheral organs, so this output fails.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo118.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

question: Which option correctly distinguishes the somatic and autonomic neural systems by the structures they supply?

options.A: Somatic: brain and spinal cord; autonomic: skeletal muscles and skin
options.B: Somatic: skeletal muscles; autonomic: involuntary organs and smooth muscles
options.C: Somatic: involuntary organs and smooth muscles; autonomic: skeletal muscles
options.D: Somatic: smooth muscles only; autonomic: skeletal and smooth muscles

correct_answer: Somatic: skeletal muscles; autonomic: involuntary organs and smooth muscles
explanation: The somatic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles; the autonomic neural system transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles.

question: When a neuron is not conducting an impulse, its axonal membrane is:

subject: Biology
question: The sodium-potassium pump of the axonal membrane transports:

options.A: 3 K+ outwards for 2 Na+ into the cell

explanation: The ionic gradients are maintained by active transport by the sodium-potassium pump, which transports 3 Na+ outwards for 2 K+ into the cell.

options.B: a positive charge on both the surfaces
options.C: a negative charge on both the surfaces
options.D: a positive outer surface and a negative inner surface

subject: Biology
question: In a diagram of impulse conduction, site X of an axon is depolarised and site Y lies immediately ahead and is still polarised. Current flows:

options.A: from Y to X on both the inner and the outer surface
options.B: from Y to X on the inner surface and from X to Y on the outer surface
options.C: from X to Y on the inner surface and from Y to X on the outer surface
options.D: from X to Y on both the inner and the outer surface

correct_answer: from X to Y on the inner surface and from Y to X on the outer surface
explanation: Inside, the positive depolarised site X drives current to site Y on the inner surface; on the outer surface current flows from Y to X to complete the circuit. This reverses polarity at Y and an action potential is generated there.

subject: Biology
question: Why does an action potential generated at one site of an axon lead to an action potential at the next site?

options.A: Neurotransmitters diffuse along the axon to the adjacent site
options.B: Current flow from the excited site reverses polarity ahead
options.C: The sodium-potassium pump pushes Na+ into the adjacent site
options.D: Outflow of K+ at the first site depolarises the adjacent site

correct_answer: Current flow from the excited site reverses polarity ahead
explanation: Current flows on the inner surface from the depolarised site to the site ahead and back on the outer surface; polarity at that site is reversed and an action potential is generated there. The sequence is repeated along the axon.

subject: Biology
question: A metabolic poison stops the sodium-potassium pump of an axon for a long period. Which change would be expected?

options.A: The Na+ and K+ gradients would gradually run down
options.B: The outside fluid would gain K+ through the pump
options.C: The membrane would at once become freely permeable to Na+
options.D: The axoplasm would steadily accumulate more K+ than before

correct_answer: The Na+ and K+ gradients would gradually run down
explanation: The ionic gradients across the resting membrane are maintained by active transport by the sodium-potassium pump. If the pump stops, these gradients would not be maintained and would run down.

question: A chemical prevents the axonal membrane from becoming permeable to Na+ when stimulated. What happens at the stimulated site?

options.A: The inner surface would become more positive than at rest
options.B: Depolarisation and an action potential would not occur
options.C: K+ would rush in and depolarise the membrane
options.D: An action potential would occur, but recovery would fail

correct_answer: Depolarisation and an action potential would not occur
explanation: Depolarisation results from the rapid influx of Na+ after the membrane becomes freely permeable to it. Without this, polarity cannot reverse and no action potential is generated.

question: A drug prevents the rise in K+ permeability that normally follows Na+ entry at a stimulated site. What is the most direct effect?

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Wind-pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence. Reason: Wind pollination is quite common in grasses.

options.A: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true, but the commonness of wind pollination in grasses does not explain why wind-pollinated flowers have single ovules and crowded inflorescences.

explanation: In the corn cob the tassels seen are the stigma and style, which wave in the wind to trap pollen grains.

subject: Biology
question: Both wind-pollinated and water-pollinated flowers are generally:

options.A: Very colourful and rich in nectar
options.B: Not very colourful and do not produce nectar
options.C: Very colourful and do not produce nectar
options.D: Not very colourful but rich in nectar

correct_answer: Not very colourful and do not produce nectar
explanation: Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar, since they need not attract animals.

question: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about:
explanation: Pollination by water is rare, limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: In water hyacinth and water lily, pollination is not brought about by water. Reason: In these plants, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: In most aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind, as in most land plants. Since the flowers are out of the water, water is not their pollinating agent. The Reason explains the Assertion.

subject: Biology
question: Which comparison of water pollination in Vallisneria and in sea grasses is correct?

options.A: In both, female flowers stay submerged and pollen is released inside water
options.B: Vallisneria pollen is released on the water surface; sea-grass pollen is released inside water
options.C: Vallisneria pollen is released inside water; sea-grass pollen is released on the water surface
options.D: In both, female flowers reach the surface and pollen floats on the surface

correct_answer: Vallisneria pollen is released on the water surface; sea-grass pollen is released inside water
explanation: In Vallisneria the female flower reaches the surface by a long stalk and male flowers or pollen are released on the surface; in sea grasses female flowers remain submerged and pollen is released inside water.

question: Statement I: Water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes among lower plant groups such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes. Statement II: Zostera is a freshwater plant in which pollen grains are released onto the surface of water.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

options.D: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

options.D: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

subject: Biology
question: In Yucca, a species of moth deposits its eggs in the locule of the ovary and the flower in turn gets pollinated by the moth. If this moth species were to disappear from a region, the most likely result is that:

options.A: Yucca shifts to wind pollination and sets seed normally
options.B: Yucca forms seeds by cleistogamy in the absence of moths
options.C: Yucca in that region cannot complete its life cycle
options.D: Yucca seed set increases as larvae no longer feed on seeds

correct_answer: Yucca in that region cannot complete its life cycle
explanation: The moth and Yucca cannot complete their life cycles without each other; the moth pollinates the flower while its larvae emerge as seeds develop.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. Floral rewards offered to animal pollinators are restricted to nectar in all species. II. In some species, the floral reward is a safe place to lay eggs. III. Pollen or nectar robbers consume pollen or nectar without bringing about pollination. IV. Insect-pollinated flowers are generally large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar. Which of the statements are correct?
explanation: Floral rewards are nectar and pollen, and in some species (Amorphophallus) a safe place to lay eggs. Robbers take rewards without pollinating. Insect-pollinated flowers are generally large, colourful, fragrant and nectar-rich.

question: Statement I: In animal-pollinated flowers, the pollen grains are generally light and non-sticky. Statement II: Small insect-pollinated flowers are always borne singly, which keeps them inconspicuous.

options.A: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

explanation: Continued self-pollination results in inbreeding depression, so flowering plants have evolved devices to discourage self-pollination.

subject: Biology
question_type: Match List I and List II
question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Monoecy; (Q) Dioecy; (R) Self-incompatibility; (S) Cleistogamy. List II: (I) Male and female flowers on the same plant, preventing autogamy but not geitonogamy; (II) Male and female flowers on different plants; (III) Genetic inhibition of self-pollen germination or pollen tube growth; (IV) Flowers that never open and are invariably autogamous. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Monoecy (castor, maize) prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy; dioecy (papaya) places sexes on different plants; self-incompatibility genetically blocks self-pollen; cleistogamy ensures autogamy.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: In papaya, both autogamy and geitonogamy are prevented. Reason: In papaya, male and female flowers are present on the same plant.

options.A: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Papaya is dioecious: male and female flowers are on different plants, which prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. The reason describes monoecy, as in castor and maize.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following act as devices that discourage self-pollination and encourage cross-pollination? I. Release of pollen before the stigma becomes receptive II. Stigma becoming receptive much before release of pollen III. Placement of anther and stigma at different positions in the flower IV. Production of cleistogamous flowers
explanation: Non-synchronised pollen release and stigma receptivity (either way) and different positions of anther and stigma discourage selfing. Cleistogamous flowers ensure autogamy.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil. Statement II: Self-incompatibility acts only against pollen from the same flower and not against pollen from other flowers of the same plant.

options.A: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.D: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Self-incompatibility prevents self-pollen, from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant, from fertilising ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or tube growth.

subject: Biology
question: In a plant with bisexual flowers, pollen placed on the stigma of the same flower or of other flowers of the same plant fails to germinate, whereas pollen from a different plant of the species germinates normally. The mechanism at work is:
explanation: Inhibition of germination of self-pollen in the pistil, with acceptance of non-self pollen, is self-incompatibility, a genetic mechanism.

subject: Biology
question: Castor and maize bear male and female flowers on the same plant. This condition:
explanation: In monoecious plants (castor, maize) unisexual flowers prevent autogamy, but pollen can reach a female flower of the same plant, so geitonogamy is possible.

subject: Biology
question: Pollen-pistil interaction refers to all the events from:

options.A: Pollen release from the anther until it lands on the stigma
options.B: Syngamy until the formation of the endosperm
options.C: Entry of the pollen tube into the ovule until syngamy
options.D: Pollen deposition on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule

correct_answer: Pollen deposition on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule
explanation: All events from deposition of pollen on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule are together referred to as pollen-pistil interaction, a dynamic process.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

subject: Biology
question: Arrange the following events after a compatible pollination in the correct order. P. Pollen tube enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus Q. Pollen grain germinates on the stigma through a germ pore R. Pollen tube grows through the tissues of stigma and style to the ovary S. Pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle
explanation: The pollen germinates on the stigma through a germ pore, the tube grows through stigma and style to the ovary, enters the ovule through the micropyle and then a synergid through the filiform apparatus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: The pistil has the ability to recognise whether a pollen grain is of the right type (compatible) or the wrong type (incompatible). Reason: Following compatible pollination, the pollen grain germinates on the stigma to produce a pollen tube through one of the germ pores.

options.A: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Recognition is mediated by chemical components of pollen interacting with those of the pistil; germination through a germ pore is an event that follows acceptance, not its explanation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: In plants which shed pollen at the two-celled stage, the generative cell divides and forms the two male gametes during the growth of the pollen tube in the stigma. Statement II: In plants which shed pollen at the three-celled condition, pollen tubes carry the two male gametes from the beginning.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: In 2-celled pollen the generative cell divides during pollen tube growth; in 3-celled pollen the two male gametes are present from the beginning.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: A student wants to observe pollen germination of pea or Vinca in the laboratory. The appropriate method is to dust pollen on a glass slide containing a drop of:

options.A: About 10 per cent sugar solution and observe after 15-30 days
options.B: About 10 per cent sugar solution and observe after 15-30 minutes
options.C: About 10 per cent salt solution and observe after 15-30 minutes
options.D: Liquid nitrogen and observe after 15-30 minutes

correct_answer: About 10 per cent sugar solution and observe after 15-30 minutes
explanation: Pollen of pea, chickpea, Crotalaria, balsam or Vinca dusted on a drop of about 10 per cent sugar solution shows pollen tubes after about 15-30 minutes under low power.

subject: Biology
question: When the pollen is of the wrong type, the pistil rejects it by: I. Preventing pollen germination on the stigma II. Preventing pollen tube growth in the style III. Dissolving the exine of the pollen with enzymes IV. Causing the pollen to divide meiotically
explanation: If the pollen is incompatible, the pistil rejects it by preventing pollen germination on the stigma or pollen tube growth in the style. No enzyme is known to degrade sporopollenin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements about pollen tube growth after compatible pollination. I. The pollen tube emerges through one of the germ pores. II. The contents of the pollen grain move into the pollen tube. III. The pollen tube enters the ovule through the chalaza. IV. The pollen tube enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus. Which of the statements are correct?
explanation: The pollen tube emerges through a germ pore, the pollen contents move into it, it enters the ovule through the micropyle and then a synergid through the filiform apparatus.

subject: Biology
question: In artificial hybridisation, removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehisces, using a pair of forceps, is called:
explanation: If the female parent bears bisexual flowers, anthers are removed from the bud before dehiscence with forceps; this is emasculation.

subject: Biology
question: In artificial hybridisation, the bag used to cover emasculated flowers is generally made of:
explanation: Emasculated flowers are covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made of butter paper, to prevent contamination of the stigma with unwanted pollen.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements about artificial hybridisation. I. Emasculation is the removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehisces. II. The bag used to cover emasculated flowers is generally made of butter paper. III. Rebagging is unnecessary once the desired pollen has been dusted. IV. Female parents with unisexual flowers must also be emasculated. Which of the statements are correct?
explanation: Anthers are removed from the bud before dehiscence; flowers are covered with butter paper bags; after dusting pollen the flowers are rebagged. Unisexual female flowers need no emasculation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Emasculation is necessary even when the female parent produces unisexual flowers. Reason: Bagging protects the stigma from contamination with unwanted pollen.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: If the female parent bears unisexual flowers there is no need for emasculation; female flower buds are bagged before they open. Bagging does protect the stigma from unwanted pollen.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

subject: Biology
question: A breeder emasculated bisexual flower buds of the female parent but forgot to bag them. Later the desired pollen was dusted on the stigmas. The main problem with the seeds obtained is that:

options.A: Some may result from unwanted pollen, so hybrid purity is not assured
options.B: No seeds can form since unbagged stigmas never become receptive
options.D: They will all be products of self-pollination

correct_answer: Some may result from unwanted pollen, so hybrid purity is not assured
explanation: Bagging prevents contamination of the stigma with unwanted pollen. Without it, foreign pollen may reach the stigma, so the progeny may not all be the intended hybrid.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

subject: Biology
question: When the female parent in a cross produces unisexual flowers, the correct procedure is to:

options.A: Pollinate the open female flowers without any bagging
options.B: Bag female buds before opening, then pollinate and rebag
options.C: Bag the male buds and leave the female flowers open
options.D: Emasculate female buds, then bag, pollinate and rebag

correct_answer: Bag female buds before opening, then pollinate and rebag
explanation: With unisexual female flowers there is no need for emasculation; female buds are bagged before opening, pollinated with desired pollen when receptive, and rebagged.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: The total number of nuclei that take part in double fertilisation in a typical angiosperm embryo sac is:

question: Assertion: The fusion of the second male gamete with the two polar nuclei is termed triple fusion. Reason: This fusion involves three haploid nuclei.

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

question: Statement I: The zygote formed by syngamy is triploid. Statement II: Double fertilisation is an event unique to flowering plants.

options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

question: Consider the following statements about embryo development. I. The embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac where the zygote is situated. II. Most zygotes divide only after a certain amount of endosperm is formed. III. The zygote first gives rise directly to a heart-shaped embryo. IV. question: Consider the following statements about apomixis. I. In some species, a diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and develops into an embryo without fertilisation. II. In many Citrus and mango varieties, some nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide, protrude into the embryo sac and develop into embryos. III. In such Citrus and mango varieties, each ovule may contain many embryos. IV. Embryos formed from nucellar cells are genetically different from the parent plant. Which of the statements are correct?
explanation: A diploid egg may form without meiosis and develop without fertilisation; more often nucellar cells develop into embryos, so each ovule has many embryos. Nucellar embryos arise from diploid maternal tissue without fertilisation, so they are not genetically new.

subject: Biology
question: A farmer grows a high-yielding hybrid crop and saves its seeds to sow the next season. The progeny is non-uniform and does not maintain the hybrid characters. If the hybrid were made apomictic, the saved seeds would:

options.A: Produce only male-sterile plants each year
options.B: Fail to germinate because they lack endosperm
options.C: Show no segregation and maintain the hybrid characters
options.D: Segregate more widely than ordinary hybrid seed

correct_answer: Show no segregation and maintain the hybrid characters
explanation: Seeds collected from hybrids segregate. If hybrids are made into apomicts, there is no segregation of characters, so farmers can use the hybrid seed year after year.

question: A student claims that in humans every step of gamete formation, in both sexes, begins only after puberty. Which observation directly contradicts this claim?

subject: Biology
question: In an experiment, the corpus luteum fails to degenerate and continues to secrete progesterone even though fertilisation has not occurred. What would be expected?

options.B: The endometrium would disintegrate faster than usual
options.C: Menstruation would begin earlier than in a usual cycle
options.D: A fresh LH surge and second ovulation would occur at once

correct_answer: The endometrium would be maintained and menstruation delayed
explanation: Progesterone from the corpus luteum maintains the endometrium. Menstruation normally follows degeneration of the corpus luteum, so continued secretion would maintain the endometrium.

question: A woman has menarche at 13 years and menopause at 50 years and is never pregnant. Assuming exactly 13 menstrual cycles per year and one ovum released per cycle, how many ova are released over this period?
explanation: Reproductive years = 50 - 13 = 37. Ova = 37 x 13 = 481, since one ovum is released in each cycle.

subject: Biology
question: After insemination, motile sperms pass through the cervix and uterus and finally reach the:

options.A: Fimbriae at the edge of the infundibulum near the ovary
options.B: Cervical canal, where they wait for the arrival of the ovum
options.C: Junction of the isthmus and ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.D: Uterine fundus, where fertilisation normally takes place

correct_answer: Junction of the isthmus and ampulla of the fallopian tube
explanation: Motile sperms swim through the cervix and uterus and reach the junction of the isthmus and ampulla (ampullary-isthmic junction); the ovum is also transported to the ampullary region.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following ensures that only one sperm can fertilise a human ovum?

options.A: Acrosomal enzymes of the first sperm that destroy all other sperms nearby
options.B: Changes in the ovum membrane, induced by sperm contact, that block more sperms
options.C: A cervical mucus plug that admits only one sperm into the uterine cavity
options.D: Fimbriae that filter sperms and allow only one of them to reach the ovum

correct_answer: Changes in the ovum membrane, induced by sperm contact, that block more sperms
explanation: During fertilisation a sperm contacts the zona pellucida and induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms, so only one sperm fertilises the ovum.

explanation: India was amongst the first countries in the world to start national level programmes for reproductive health; these family planning programmes were initiated in 1951 and periodically assessed over the following decades. MTP was legalised later, in 1971.

question: Improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas, currently in operation in India, are popularly known as:

options.B: Maternal Nutrition and Child Feeding programmes
options.D: Reproductive and Child Health Care programmes

correct_answer: Reproductive and Child Health Care programmes
explanation: The family planning programmes initiated in 1951 were improved to cover wider reproduction-related areas and are now run under the popular name Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: India was amongst the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a national level to attain total reproductive health as a social goal. Statement II: The family planning programmes of India, once initiated, were never assessed or modified over the following decades.

options.A: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: India started national level programmes for total reproductive health very early, from 1951. These programmes were periodically assessed and improved, leading to the present RCH programmes, so Statement II is incorrect.

subject: Biology
question: With respect to creating awareness among people about reproduction-related aspects, consider the following: I. Audio-visual and print media are used for the purpose. II. Governmental and non-governmental agencies take part in it. III. Parents, close relatives, teachers and friends have a major role in giving such information. IV. Information on sex-related aspects should be withheld from young people until marriage. Which of the statements are correct?
explanation: Awareness is created with the help of audio-visual and print media, governmental and non-governmental agencies, and parents, close relatives, teachers and friends play a major role. The strategy encourages giving right information to the young, not withholding it.

question: Introduction of sex education in schools is encouraged mainly to:

options.A: Replace the role of parents in such matters
options.C: Give right information and dispel myths about sex
options.D: Train students to perform contraceptive procedures

correct_answer: Give right information and dispel myths about sex
explanation: Sex education in schools provides right information to the young and discourages children from believing in myths and misconceptions about sex-related aspects. Parents, teachers and others continue to play a role.

explanation: Young people should get proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, and sexually transmitted infections including AIDS, so that they lead a reproductively healthy life.

subject: Biology
question: Fertile couples and people in the marriageable age group should be educated about which of the following? I. Available birth control options. II. Routine use of amniocentesis to know the sex of the foetus. III. Importance of breast feeding and post-natal care of mother and child. IV. Equal opportunities for the male and the female child. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Couples are educated about birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of mother and child, importance of breast feeding and equal opportunities for the male and the female child. Use of amniocentesis for sex determination is banned by law, so it is not part of such education.

options.A: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

question: The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination in India was imposed mainly to:

options.C: Prevent spread of STIs through amniotic fluid
options.D: Reduce the cost of antenatal care

explanation: The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination was imposed to legally check the increasing female foeticides, as sex determination was frequently followed by abortion of female foetuses.

subject: Biology
question: A student claims that the statutory ban on amniocentesis in India prohibits the technique for every purpose. The correct position is that the ban is specifically against its use for:

options.A: Pregnancies conceived through IVF and embryo transfer
options.B: Determining the sex of the unborn child
options.C: Any examination of the foetus in the second trimester
options.D: Mothers below the legal age of marriage

correct_answer: Determining the sex of the unborn child
explanation: The statutory ban is on amniocentesis for sex determination. Its misuse to find the sex of the unborn child, frequently followed by MTP if the foetus is female, is against the law and promotes female foeticide.

question: Which of the following indicate improved reproductive health of a society? I. Better awareness about sex-related matters. II. Decreased maternal and infant mortality rates. III. Increased number of couples with large families. IV. Better detection and cure of STDs. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Improved reproductive health is indicated by better awareness about sex-related matters, more medically assisted deliveries, better post-natal care with decreased maternal and infant mortality, an increased number of couples with small families and better detection and cure of STDs. question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of an ideal contraceptive?

options.B: Effective with no or least side-effects
options.D: No interference with sexual drive or act

explanation: An ideal contraceptive should be user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible with no or least side-effects, and should not interfere with sexual drive, desire or the sexual act. Irreversibility is a feature of sterilisation, not of an ideal contraceptive.

question: Assertion: An ideal contraceptive should be reversible. Reason: An ideal contraceptive should in no way interfere with the sexual drive, desire and/or the sexual act of the user.

subject: Biology
question: In periodic abstinence, couples avoid coitus from:

options.A: Day 1 to 5 of the menstrual cycle
options.B: Day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle
options.C: Day 18 to 28 of the menstrual cycle
options.D: Day 5 to 9 of the menstrual cycle

correct_answer: Day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle
explanation: Ovulation can be expected from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle, called the fertile period. Couples avoid coitus during these days to prevent conception.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Avoiding coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle can prevent conception. Reason: Ovulation could be expected during these days, so the period is called the fertile period.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Since ovulation is expected from day 10 to 17, avoiding coitus during this fertile period reduces chances of ovum and sperm meeting. The reason directly explains the assertion.

subject: Biology
question: In coitus interruptus, conception is avoided because:

options.A: The male withdraws the penis just before ejaculation
options.B: A rubber barrier covers the cervix during coitus
options.C: The couple abstains from coitus during the fertile period
options.D: Ovulation does not occur during intense lactation

correct_answer: The male withdraws the penis just before ejaculation
explanation: Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is a natural method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Lactational amenorrhoea can serve as a natural contraceptive method following parturition. Reason: It remains effective as long as the mother breast-feeds, even for two years or more.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Ovulation and the cycle do not occur during intense lactation after parturition, so chances of conception are almost nil while the mother breast-feeds fully. However, the method is effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition, so the reason is false.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: Lactational amenorrhoea is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Statement II: Since no medicines or devices are used in natural methods, their chances of failure are very low.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Lactational amenorrhoea relies on absence of ovulation during intense lactation. In natural methods no medicines or devices are used, so side effects are almost nil, but the chances of failure are high. Statement II confuses side effects with failure rate.

subject: Biology
question: A mother who is fully breast-feeding her baby believes she cannot conceive at all as long as she continues breast-feeding. Which statement about lactational amenorrhoea correctly corrects her?

options.A: It works only if oral pills are taken alongside
options.B: It is effective only during the first week after delivery
options.C: It is effective only up to six months after parturition
options.D: It acts by blocking sperm entry through the cervix

correct_answer: It is effective only up to six months after parturition
explanation: Lactational amenorrhoea depends on absence of ovulation during intense lactation following parturition. It is effective only up to a maximum period of six months after parturition, and its chances of failure are high.

question: Consider the following statements about condoms: I. They are made of thin rubber or latex sheath. II. They are used to cover the penis in the male or the vagina and cervix in the female just before coitus. III. They protect the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. IV. They are reusable after proper washing. Which statements are correct?
explanation: Condoms are thin rubber or latex sheaths that cover the penis or the vagina and cervix so that ejaculated semen does not enter the female reproductive tract. They also protect against STIs and AIDS. Both male and female condoms are disposable.

Reason: If a pregnancy has lasted more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks, two registered medical practitioners must be of the opinion, formed in good faith, that the required grounds exist.

options.A: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: One practitioner's opinion suffices only within the first 12 weeks. A 16-week pregnancy falls between 12 and 24 weeks, which needs the opinion of two registered medical practitioners. The assertion is false and the reason is true.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following are grounds stated for termination of pregnancy under the MTP (Amendment) Act? I. Continuation of the pregnancy would involve a risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to her physical or mental health. II. There is a substantial risk that the child, if born, would suffer from such physical or mental abnormalities as to be seriously handicapped. III. The foetus has been found to be female by amniocentesis. Choose the correct option.
explanation: The two grounds are risk to the life or grave injury to the physical or mental health of the pregnant woman, and a substantial risk of serious physical or mental abnormality in the child. MTP after sex determination of a female foetus is totally against the law.

question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Early symptoms of STIs; (Q) Later complications of untreated STIs; (R) Age group with very high incidence; (S) Guiding principle in tackling STIs. List II: (I) 15 to 24 years; (II) Prevention is better than cure; (III) Itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings in genital region; (IV) PID, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Early symptoms are minor: itching, fluid discharge, slight pain and swellings in the genital region. Untreated infections can lead to PID, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract. options.B: Use oral pills during every coitus
options.C: Always try to use condoms during coitus

correct_answer: Always try to use condoms during coitus
explanation: To be free of STIs: avoid sex with unknown partners or multiple partners, always try to use condoms during coitus, and in case of doubt go to a qualified doctor for early detection and complete treatment.

question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Male partner unable to inseminate the female; (Q) Female cannot produce ova but can provide suitable environment for fertilisation; (R) Embryo with more than 8 blastomeres ready for transfer; (S) Sperm to be injected directly into the ovum in the laboratory. List II: (I) IUT; (II) ICSI; (III) Artificial insemination; (IV) GIFT. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Artificial insemination helps when the male cannot inseminate the female or has very low sperm counts. GIFT transfers a donor ovum into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce one. Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus by IUT. ICSI injects a sperm directly into the ovum.

subject: Biology
question: A young man suspects that he may have contracted an STI after unprotected intercourse, but he has no symptoms. Which course of action is correct?

options.A: Wait for symptoms to appear, as an STI without symptoms causes no harm
options.B: Consult a qualified doctor for early detection and complete the treatment
options.C: Use a condom from now on, as this will also clear any existing infection
options.D: Avoid testing, since no STI can be cured even when it is detected early

correct_answer: Consult a qualified doctor for early detection and complete the treatment
explanation: In case of doubt one should go to a qualified doctor for early detection and get complete treatment if diagnosed with infection. Early symptoms of STIs are often minor or absent, but untreated infections can lead to complications such as pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility. Most STIs, except hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV, are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

explanation: Pills act hormonally and do not form any barrier against pathogens. Condoms have the additional benefit of protecting the user from STIs and AIDS.

question: Assertion: When Mendel crossed true-breeding tall and dwarf pea plants, all F1 plants were tall and none was of intermediate height. Reason: In a dissimilar pair of factors, one member of the pair dominates the other.

explanation: The F1 plants of a tall x dwarf cross were all tall, resembling one parent, with no blending. This is explained by dominance: in the heterozygote Tt, the factor T dominates t, so only the tall trait is expressed.

question: Mendel proposed that something was being stably passed down, unchanged, from parent to offspring through the gametes. What did he call these things, and what are they called today?

options.A: He called them genes; today they are called factors
options.B: He called them alleles; today they are called loci
options.C: He called them chromosomes; today they are called alleles
options.D: He called them factors; today they are called genes

correct_answer: He called them factors; today they are called genes
explanation: Mendel called the units of inheritance factors. Now we call them genes; genes are the units of inheritance containing the information required to express a particular trait.

question: In the F2 generation of a cross between true-breeding tall (TT) and dwarf (tt) pea plants, what fraction of the tall plants is expected to be true-breeding?

explanation: Among tall F2 plants, 1/3 are TT and give no dwarfs, while 2/3 are Tt and give 1/4 dwarfs on selfing. Dwarf fraction = 2/3 x 1/4 = 1/6.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following form part of the law of dominance as stated by Mendel? I. Characters are controlled by discrete units called factors. II. Factors occur in pairs. III. In a dissimilar pair of factors, one member of the pair dominates the other. IV. In a dissimilar pair of factors, the two factors blend to give an intermediate trait.
explanation: The law of dominance states that characters are controlled by discrete factors, that factors occur in pairs, and that in a dissimilar pair one factor dominates the other. Mendel found no blending.

question: Assertion: A heterozygous pea plant (Tt) produces two kinds of gametes, each in equal proportion. Reason: A homozygous parent produces all gametes that are similar.

options.A: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: By the law of segregation, a heterozygote produces T and t gametes in equal proportion, and a homozygote produces only one type of gamete. Both are true, but the homozygote fact does not explain the heterozygote's behaviour; the explanation is segregation of the two factors.

options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The law of segregation is based on the fact that alleles do not blend, and both characters are recovered as such in F2. Because each gamete receives only one factor, t gametes from F1 can unite to form tt dwarf plants.

subject: Biology
question: A gene codes for an enzyme. Consider the following statements about a heterozygote carrying one unmodified allele and one modified allele. I. If the modified allele produces a normal or less efficient enzyme, it may be equivalent to the unmodified allele and produce the same phenotype. II. If the modified allele produces a non-functional enzyme or no enzyme, the phenotype depends only on the functioning of the unmodified allele. III. The unmodified, functioning allele, which represents the original phenotype, is usually the recessive allele. IV. The modified allele is generally the recessive allele. Which statements are correct?
explanation: A modified allele may give a normal or less efficient enzyme (equivalent phenotype), a non-functional enzyme or no enzyme. In the latter cases, the phenotype depends only on the unmodified allele. The unmodified, functioning allele is dominant and the modified allele is usually recessive.

subject: Biology
question: In pea, starch synthesis is controlled by one gene with alleles B and b. BB seeds synthesise starch effectively and have large starch grains; bb seeds have small starch grains. After maturation, BB seeds are round and bb seeds wrinkled. Bb seeds are round but have starch grains of intermediate size. Which conclusion follows?

options.A: Incomplete dominance for seed shape but complete dominance for grain size
options.B: Co-dominance for seed shape and complete dominance for grain size
options.C: Complete dominance for seed shape but incomplete dominance for grain size
options.D: Complete dominance of B for both seed shape and for grain size

correct_answer: Complete dominance for seed shape but incomplete dominance for grain size
explanation: Bb seeds are round, so B behaves as dominant for seed shape. Their starch grains are intermediate in size, so for grain size the alleles show incomplete dominance. Dominance therefore depends on the gene product and the phenotype chosen; it is not an autonomous feature of a gene.

explanation: Expected numbers: round yellow 9/16 x 1600 = 900; wrinkled green 1/16 x 1600 = 100; round green 3/16 x 1600 = 300. RrYy is 4/16 x 1600 = 400, not 200.

subject: Biology
question: Among the F2 plants with round, yellow seeds from a dihybrid cross RRYY x rryy, what fraction is heterozygous at both loci?
explanation: Round yellow plants form 9 of 16 combinations: RRYY 1, RRYy 2, RrYY 2, RrYy 4. So RrYy among them = 4/9.

subject: Biology
question: For the F2 obtained by selfing a dihybrid pea plant RrYy: Statement I: The probability of a plant with genotype RRYy is 1/8. Statement II: The probability of a plant with genotype RrYy is 1/16.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: RRYy: P(RR) = 1/4 and P(Yy) = 1/2, giving 1/8. RrYy: P(Rr) = 1/2 and P(Yy) = 1/2, giving 1/4, not 1/16.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: The dihybrid F2 phenotypic ratio of 9:3:3:1 can be derived as the product of two monohybrid ratios, (3:1) x (3:1). Reason: When two pairs of traits are combined in a hybrid, segregation of one pair of characters is independent of the other pair.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Each gene alone gives 3:1 in F2. Because the two pairs segregate independently, the combined ratio is the product (3 round : 1 wrinkled) x (3 yellow : 1 green) = 9:3:3:1.

question: A pea plant RrYy is crossed with an rryy plant. What fraction of the progeny shows exactly one dominant trait, either round or yellow but not both?
explanation: The test cross gives four equal classes: round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow and wrinkled green, each 1/4. Round green and wrinkled yellow together = 1/2.

options.C: 1 round yellow : 1 round green : 1 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green

explanation: RrYY produces RY and rY gametes in equal proportion, and rryy produces only ry. Offspring are RrYy (round yellow) and rrYy (wrinkled yellow) in 1:1. All are yellow because the parent is YY.

subject: Biology
question: An organism of genotype AaBbCc, with the three genes assorting independently, is self-fertilised. What are the number of genetically different gametes it can form and the probability of an aabbcc offspring?
explanation: Number of gamete types = 2^3 = 8. Each recessive homozygote has a probability of 1/4, so aabbcc = (1/4)^3 = 1/64.

question: Statement I: Mendel published his work on inheritance of characters in 1865, but it remained unrecognised till 1900. Statement II: One reason was that Mendel's approach of using mathematics to explain biological phenomena was totally new and unacceptable to many biologists of his time.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Mendel published his work in 1865 and it remained unrecognised till 1900. The reasons included poor communication, non-acceptance of discrete factors as an explanation of continuous variation, a mathematical approach new to biologists, and lack of physical proof for factors.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following were reasons why Mendel's work remained unrecognised for a long time? I. Communication was not easy in those days, so his work could not be widely publicised. II. His concept of genes as stable, discrete units was not accepted as an explanation for the apparently continuous variation seen in nature. III. He could not provide any physical proof for the existence of factors or say what they were made of. IV. His results could not be repeated because garden pea is naturally cross-pollinated.
explanation: Statements I, II and III are among the reasons for non-recognition. Statement IV is wrong: pea was suitable because true-breeding lines could be obtained through self-pollination.

subject: Biology
question: Who united the knowledge of chromosomal segregation with Mendelian principles and called it the chromosomal theory of inheritance?
explanation: Sutton and Boveri noted the parallel behaviour of chromosomes and genes. Sutton united chromosomal segregation with Mendelian principles and called it the chromosomal theory of inheritance. Morgan later verified it experimentally.

Choose the correct option.
explanation: Henking (1891) observed the X body. Sutton and Boveri noted the parallel between chromosomes and genes. Morgan verified the chromosomal theory with Drosophila. His student Sturtevant mapped genes using recombination frequency.

It completes its life cycle in about two weeks. III. A single mating produces a large number of progeny flies. IV. Male and female flies cannot be easily distinguished.
explanation: Drosophila grows on simple synthetic medium, completes its life cycle in about two weeks, and a single mating produces many progeny. There is clear differentiation of the sexes, so males and females are easily distinguishable; statement IV is false.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Sutton and Boveri argued that the pairing and separation of a pair of chromosomes would lead to the segregation of a pair of factors they carried. Reason: They noted that the behaviour of chromosomes during meiosis was parallel to the behaviour of genes.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: By 1902 chromosome movement during meiosis had been worked out. Seeing that chromosomes and genes both occur in pairs and segregate at gamete formation, Sutton and Boveri used chromosome movement to explain Mendel's laws.

subject: Biology
question: Morgan crossed yellow-bodied, white-eyed female Drosophila with brown-bodied, red-eyed males and intercrossed their F1 progeny. What did he observe in F2?

options.A: Only parental combinations appeared in F2, and no recombinant flies were produced at all
options.B: The two genes segregated independently of each other, giving an F2 ratio close to 9:3:3:1
options.C: The two genes did not segregate independently, and the F2 ratio deviated very significantly from 9:3:3:1
options.D: The two genes showed incomplete dominance, so the F2 ratio changed from 9:3:3:1 to 1:2:1

correct_answer: The two genes did not segregate independently, and the F2 ratio deviated very significantly from 9:3:3:1
explanation: Morgan's dihybrid crosses with sex-linked genes showed that the two genes did not segregate independently and the F2 ratio deviated very significantly from 9:3:3:1. Parental combinations were much more frequent than non-parental ones.

options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.D: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Morgan used linkage for the physical association of genes on a chromosome and recombination for the generation of non-parental gene combinations. Statement II wrongly says parental.

question: Match List I with List II for Morgan's dihybrid crosses in Drosophila. List I: (P) Recombinants for genes white and yellow; (Q) Recombinants for genes white and miniature wing; (R) Parental types for genes white and yellow; (S) Parental types for genes white and miniature wing. List II: (I) 37.2 per cent; (II) 98.7 per cent; (III) 1.3 per cent; (IV) 62.8 per cent. Choose the correct option.
explanation: White and yellow were very tightly linked, with 1.3 per cent recombination and therefore 98.7 per cent parental types. White and miniature wing showed 37.2 per cent recombination and 62.8 per cent parental types.

subject: Biology
question: In Drosophila, genes white and yellow showed 1.3 per cent recombination, whereas genes white and miniature wing showed 37.2 per cent recombination. Which comparison is correct?

options.A: White and yellow are very tightly linked, while white and miniature wing are loosely linked and lie farther apart
options.B: Both gene pairs assort independently, since both show some recombination
options.C: White and miniature wing are on different chromosomes, while white and yellow are on the same chromosome
options.D: White and yellow lie farther apart than white and miniature wing

correct_answer: White and yellow are very tightly linked, while white and miniature wing are loosely linked and lie farther apart
explanation: Low recombination means tight linkage and genes close together; higher recombination means loose linkage and genes farther apart. All three genes are X-linked.

subject: Biology
question: Three linked genes m, n and o show the following recombination frequencies: m and n, 5 per cent; n and o, 3 per cent; m and o, 8 per cent. Using recombination frequency as a measure of distance, what is the order of the genes?

options.A: n lies between m and o
options.B: o lies between m and n
options.C: The order cannot be judged from these data
options.D: m lies between n and o

correct_answer: n lies between m and o
explanation: The largest value, 8 per cent between m and o, equals 5 + 3, the sum of the other two. So m and o are at the ends and n lies between them: m, 5, n, 3, o.

subject: Biology
question: Two genes on the same chromosome show 20 per cent recombination. An individual heterozygous for both genes is test crossed. What percentage of the progeny is expected in each of the two parental classes?
explanation: Recombinants total 20 per cent, split equally between two recombinant classes (10 per cent each). Parentals total 80 per cent, split equally into two classes of 40 per cent each.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Some genes on the same chromosome are very tightly linked and show very low recombination, while others are loosely linked. Reason: Morgan attributed the higher proportion of parental gene combinations to the physical association of genes on a chromosome.

options.A: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Morgan explained excess parental types as linkage. Differences in linkage strength are explained by distance between genes, which Sturtevant used for mapping, not by the mere fact of physical association.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: In Morgan's experiments, the genes white and miniature wing showed 37.2 per cent recombination. Reason: The genes white and miniature wing are located on different chromosomes.

options.A: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: White and miniature wing are both on the X chromosome and are loosely linked, giving 37.2 per cent recombination. Genes on different chromosomes would assort independently.

subject: Biology
question: Mendel's dihybrid crosses in pea gave 9:3:3:1, whereas Morgan's dihybrid crosses involving body colour and eye colour in Drosophila deviated very significantly from it. What best explains this difference?

options.A: Dominance does not operate in Drosophila, so F2 phenotypes cannot be grouped as in pea
options.B: Drosophila does not undergo meiosis in the same way as pea, so its genes segregate differently
options.C: The genes in Morgan's crosses were located on the same chromosome, while those in Mendel's crosses assorted independently
options.D: Morgan's sample sizes were too small to give Mendelian ratios reliably in the F2 generation

correct_answer: The genes in Morgan's crosses were located on the same chromosome, while those in Mendel's crosses assorted independently
explanation: Morgan's genes were on the X chromosome. Being linked, they did not assort independently, so parental combinations were much more frequent than non-parental ones.

question: Match List I with List II for human skin colour, assumed to be controlled by three genes A, B and C with additive dominant alleles. List I: (P) AABBCC; (Q) aabbcc; (R) AaBbCc; (S) Number of phenotypic classes among offspring of AaBbCc x AaBbCc. List II: (I) Seven; (II) Lightest skin colour; (III) Darkest skin colour; (IV) Intermediate skin colour. Choose the correct option.

subject: Biology
question: Two persons of genotype AaBbCc for skin colour (three genes, additive alleles, independent assortment) have children. What fraction of the children is expected to have the same skin colour as the parents?
explanation: The parents carry three dominant alleles each. The number of ways to have exactly three dominant alleles among six is 20, out of 64 combinations, so the fraction is 20/64.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: In human skin colour, an individual of genotype AaBbCc has the darkest skin colour. Statement II: In a polygenic trait, the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele, the effect of each allele being additive.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.D: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

explanation: AaBbCc has three dominant alleles. AABbcc and aaBBCc also have three. AABBcc has four and AaBbcc has two.

subject: Biology
question: The basis of pleiotropism in most cases is

options.A: the additive effect of several genes, each contributing to a single phenotype
options.B: the presence of more than two alleles of a single gene in a population
options.C: the physical association of several different genes on the same chromosome
options.D: the effect of a gene on metabolic pathways which contribute towards different phenotypes

correct_answer: the effect of a gene on metabolic pathways which contribute towards different phenotypes
explanation: A single gene can exhibit multiple phenotypic expressions. In most cases this is because the gene affects metabolic pathways that contribute to different phenotypes, as in phenylketonuria.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements about phenylketonuria as an example of pleiotropy. I. It is caused by mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase. II. It is a single gene mutation. III. It manifests through mental retardation and a reduction in hair and skin pigmentation. IV. It is caused by an additional copy of an autosome. Which of the statements are correct?
explanation: Phenylketonuria results from a single gene mutation in the gene for phenylalanine hydroxylase, and shows mental retardation along with reduced hair and skin pigmentation. It is a Mendelian, not chromosomal, disorder.

question: Assertion: Phenylketonuria shows reduced hair and skin pigmentation in addition to mental retardation. Reason: In phenylketonuria, phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives are excreted in urine because of their poor absorption by the kidney.

question: Consider the following statements about the F2 of Mendel's dihybrid cross RRYY x rryy. I. Nine different genotypes are produced. II. Plants of genotype RRYY and RrYy occur in the ratio 1:2. III. Plants with non-parental phenotypes (round green and wrinkled yellow) together form 6/16. IV. Plants homozygous at both loci together form 1/4. Which statements are correct?
explanation: There are nine genotypes. RRYY is 1/16 and RrYy 4/16, a ratio of 1:4. Round green (3/16) plus wrinkled yellow (3/16) = 6/16. RRYY, RRyy, rrYY and rryy are each 1/16, totalling 4/16 = 1/4.

subject: Biology
question: A test cross of a dihybrid gives four progeny classes in the proportions 42 per cent, 42 per cent, 8 per cent and 8 per cent, the two larger classes having the parental combinations. Which conclusion is correct?

options.A: The genes assort independently, as four classes are produced
options.B: The genes are linked, with a recombination frequency of 16 per cent
options.C: The genes are linked, with a recombination frequency of 8 per cent
options.D: The genes are linked, with a recombination frequency of 84 per cent

correct_answer: The genes are linked, with a recombination frequency of 16 per cent
explanation: Parental combinations far exceed non-parental ones, showing linkage. Recombination frequency = 8 + 8 = 16 per cent.

subject: Biology
question: A diagram shows two pairs of homologous chromosomes, each carrying a different gene, at metaphase I of meiosis. It shows two equally likely alternative arrangements of the pairs at the equator, leading to four kinds of gametes in equal frequency. This diagram illustrates the chromosomal basis of

options.A: linkage of genes on one chromosome

explanation: Independent orientation of different chromosome pairs at metaphase I, followed by their separation at anaphase I, lets alleles of genes on different chromosomes assort independently, giving four gamete types in equal frequency.

subject: Biology
question: In 1891, Henking traced a specific nuclear structure through spermatogenesis in a few insects and found that 50 per cent of the sperm received it. What did he name this structure?
explanation: Henking (1891) observed that a specific nuclear structure was received by only half the sperm. He could not explain its significance and named it the X body; it was later found to be a chromosome and named the X chromosome.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: Henking could not explain the significance of the nuclear structure he observed in some sperm of a few insects. Statement II: Further investigations showed that this structure was in fact a chromosome, which was therefore named the X chromosome.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Henking could not explain the significance of the structure and called it the X body. Later work showed it to be a chromosome, hence the name X chromosome.

subject: Biology
question: In grasshopper, all eggs bear an additional X chromosome besides the autosomes, while some sperm bear an X chromosome and some do not. This mechanism of sex determination is
explanation: Grasshopper is an example of XO type sex determination. Eggs fertilised by sperm having an X chromosome become females, and those fertilised by sperm lacking the X chromosome become males.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: In an insect with XO type sex determination, the somatic cells of females contain 24 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are present in the somatic cells of males?
explanation: Females have 22 autosomes plus XX = 24. Males have the same 22 autosomes but only one X chromosome, so they have 23 chromosomes, one less than females.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: In grasshopper, males have the same number of chromosomes as females. Reason: In grasshopper, some sperm bear the X chromosome while others do not.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: In grasshopper, males have only one X chromosome besides the autosomes, so they have one chromosome less than females. Some sperm carry the X and some do not, which is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)

question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Females produce two different types of gametes in terms of sex chromosomes; (Q) Males have one chromosome less than females; (R) Male heterogamety with XY males, in an insect; (S) Sex of the child is decided by the sperm, as the mother contributes only an X chromosome. List II: (I) Humans; (II) Birds; (III) Grasshopper; (IV) Drosophila. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Birds show female heterogamety (ZW females). Grasshopper is XO, males having one chromosome less. Drosophila is an insect with XY males. In humans, the father's sperm (X or Y) decides the sex of the child.
