subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Restriction enzymes are placed among the endonucleases. Reason: Endonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Restriction enzymes cut at specific positions within DNA, so they are endonucleases. The Reason is false: removal of nucleotides from the ends is done by exonucleases.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)

subject: Biology
question: Which option correctly compares the origin of replication (ori) and the selectable marker of a cloning vector?

options.A: Ori helps identify and eliminate non-transformants; the selectable marker starts replication and controls copy number
options.B: Both start replication, but only the selectable marker controls copy number
options.C: Ori starts replication and controls copy number; the selectable marker helps identify and eliminate non-transformants
options.D: Ori provides unique restriction sites; the selectable marker produces sticky ends

correct_answer: Ori starts replication and controls copy number; the selectable marker helps identify and eliminate non-transformants
explanation: The ori is the sequence from where replication starts and it controls the copy number of linked DNA. The selectable marker, usually an antibiotic resistance gene, lets transformants grow and eliminates non-transformants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: Once a restriction endonuclease finds its specific recognition sequence, it binds to the DNA and cuts:

options.A: glycosidic bonds between sugars and bases on one strand
options.B: each of the two strands at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones
options.C: only one strand by breaking hydrogen bonds between bases
options.D: both strands by breaking hydrogen bonds between complementary bases

correct_answer: each of the two strands at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones
explanation: A restriction endonuclease cuts each strand of the double helix at specific points in the sugar-phosphate backbone, that is, it breaks phosphodiester linkages, not hydrogen bonds.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: Which statement correctly defines a palindromic sequence in DNA?

options.A: A short sequence of base pairs repeated many times in tandem on one strand of the DNA
options.B: A sequence of base pairs that reads the same on the two strands when the orientation of reading is kept the same
options.C: A sequence on one strand that reads the same from left to right and from right to left
options.D: A sequence in which both strands carry identical bases at each position along the stretch

correct_answer: A sequence of base pairs that reads the same on the two strands when the orientation of reading is kept the same
explanation: In DNA, a palindrome is a base pair sequence that reads the same on both strands when each is read in the same orientation, for example 5' GAATTC 3' on both strands. It is not a single-strand mirror like the word MALAYALAM.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: Only one strand of each double-stranded sequence is shown (5' to 3'). Which of them is a palindromic sequence?
explanation: The complementary strand of 5' GGATCC 3' is 3' CCTAGG 5', which read 5' to 3' is GGATCC, identical to the first strand. The other sequences give different complementary sequences when read in the same orientation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: Restriction enzymes such as EcoR I cut the DNA strands:

options.A: exactly at the centre of the palindrome, so that both strands are cut at the same level
options.B: at random points outside the recognition sequence, at a different place on each strand
options.C: between different pairs of bases on the two strands, unrelated to the palindrome
options.D: a little away from the centre of the palindrome, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands

correct_answer: a little away from the centre of the palindrome, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands
explanation: The cut is made a little away from the centre of the palindrome but between the same two bases on both strands. This staggered cut leaves single-stranded overhangs, the sticky ends.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: The overhanging single-stranded stretches left after EcoR I cuts DNA are called sticky ends. Reason: These stretches form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The ends are named sticky because their single-stranded overhangs base pair by hydrogen bonds with complementary cut ends. This stickiness helps DNA ligase to join them.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: The stickiness of the ends produced by restriction enzymes facilitates the action of the enzyme DNA ligase. Statement II: DNA from different sources always gets the same kind of sticky ends, whichever restriction enzymes are used to cut it.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.D: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Sticky ends pair with complementary ends, bringing fragments together for ligase. Only DNA cut with the same restriction enzyme gives the same kind of sticky ends; different enzymes generally give different ends.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
subtopic: Same enzyme for vector and source
question: Assertion: Normally, a recombinant vector molecule cannot be created unless the vector and the source DNA are cut with the same restriction enzyme. Reason: DNA fragments cut by the same restriction enzyme have the same kind of sticky ends, which can be joined end to end by DNA ligase.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Joining requires complementary overhangs. Cutting both vector and source DNA with the same enzyme produces matching sticky ends, which pair and are sealed by ligase. The Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: A double-stranded segment 5' GAATTC 3' / 3' CTTAAG 5' is cut by EcoR I between G and A on each strand. Which description of the resulting ends is correct?

options.A: Both fragments carry a single-stranded overhang reading 5' AATT 3'
options.B: Both fragments have blunt ends with no overhang
options.C: Both fragments carry a single-base overhang reading 5' G 3'
options.D: One fragment carries 5' AATT 3' and the other carries 5' TTAA 3'

correct_answer: Both fragments carry a single-stranded overhang reading 5' AATT 3'
explanation: Cutting between G and A on both strands leaves G on one side and AATTC on the other on each strand. Each fragment therefore has a four-base 5' overhang that reads AATT 5' to 3', and these overhangs are complementary to each other.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

subject: Biology
question: The term 'molecular scissors' refers to:
explanation: Cutting DNA at specific locations became possible with the discovery of 'molecular scissors', the restriction enzymes. Ligase joins fragments, while polymerase synthesises DNA.

subject: Biology
question: During gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the:

options.A: anode, because DNA fragments are positively charged
options.B: cathode, because DNA fragments are negatively charged
options.C: cathode, because DNA fragments are positively charged
options.D: anode, because DNA fragments are negatively charged

correct_answer: anode, because DNA fragments are negatively charged
explanation: The phosphate groups make DNA negatively charged, so in an electric field DNA fragments move towards the anode (positive electrode) through the gel matrix.

subject: Biology
question: The most commonly used matrix for separating DNA fragments by electrophoresis is:

options.A: cellulose, a natural polymer extracted from cotton
options.B: agarose, a synthetic polymer made in the laboratory
options.C: agarose, a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds
options.D: chitin, a natural polymer extracted from fungi

correct_answer: agarose, a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds
explanation: Agarose, a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds, is the most commonly used matrix. It provides a sieving effect that separates DNA fragments by size.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: In agarose gel electrophoresis, larger DNA fragments move farther from the wells than smaller ones. Reason: DNA fragments separate according to their size through the sieving effect of the agarose gel.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The agarose gel acts as a sieve, so smaller fragments pass through more easily and move farther. The Assertion reverses this, while the Reason is true.

subject: Biology
question: Separated DNA fragments in an agarose gel are visualised as:

options.A: blue bands in visible light after staining with ethidium bromide
options.B: bright orange bands in visible light without any staining
options.C: bright orange bands under UV light after staining with ethidium bromide
options.D: green bands under UV light after staining with iodine

correct_answer: bright orange bands under UV light after staining with ethidium bromide
explanation: Pure DNA fragments cannot be seen in visible light without staining. After ethidium bromide staining and exposure to UV radiation, DNA appears as bright orange bands.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: Pure DNA fragments separated on agarose gel can be seen in visible light without staining. Statement II: Cutting out the separated bands of DNA from the agarose gel and extracting them from the gel piece is called elution.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.D: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: DNA cannot be seen without staining with ethidium bromide and exposure to UV light. Cutting out bands and extracting DNA from the gel pieces is elution; the purified fragments are then joined with cloning vectors.

Loading digested DNA in agarose gel and applying an electric field R. Cutting out the desired band and extracting DNA from the gel piece S. Joining the purified fragment with a cloning vector

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. Each restriction endonuclease recognises a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA. II. Hind II cuts DNA molecules at random points. III. The Roman numeral in a restriction enzyme's name indicates the order in which it was isolated from that strain. IV. Restriction enzymes cut at the exact centre of the palindrome on both strands, producing sticky ends. Which of the above statements are correct?
explanation: Restriction enzymes recognise specific palindromes, and the Roman numeral shows the order of isolation. Hind II always cuts at a particular point in its six base pair recognition sequence, not randomly, and cuts are made a little away from the centre to leave sticky ends.

question_type: Match List I and List II
question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Exonuclease; (Q) Endonuclease; (R) DNA ligase; (S) Thermostable DNA polymerase. List II: (I) Joins the ends of cut DNA molecules; (II) Makes cuts at specific positions within the DNA; (III) Removes nucleotides from the ends of the DNA; (IV) Extends primers in repeated high-temperature cycles. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from ends, endonucleases cut within DNA at specific positions, ligase joins cut ends, and thermostable DNA polymerase extends primers during PCR.

subject: Biology
question: A linear DNA molecule and a circular plasmid each have three recognition sites for EcoR I. On complete digestion with EcoR I, how many fragments will be obtained from the linear molecule and the circular plasmid, respectively?
explanation: n cuts in a linear molecule give n + 1 fragments, so three cuts give four. A circle has no free ends, so n cuts give n fragments, that is, three. This is why multiple sites in a vector generate several fragments and complicate cloning.

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In EcoR I, 'co' is the species and R comes from the strain RY 13. Restriction enzymes are nucleases, a class that includes exonucleases and endonucleases.

subject: Biology
question: Which option correctly compares plasmids and bacteriophages as cloning vectors?

options.C: Both replicate independently of chromosomal control, and bacteriophages reach very high genome copy numbers because of their high number per cell
options.D: Both replicate independently of chromosomal control, but plasmids always reach higher copy numbers than bacteriophages

correct_answer: Both replicate independently of chromosomal control, and bacteriophages reach very high genome copy numbers because of their high number per cell
explanation: Plasmids and bacteriophages can replicate within bacterial cells independent of chromosomal DNA. Because phages are present in high numbers per cell, their genomes reach very high copy numbers; plasmid copy numbers vary from one or two to 15 to 100 or more per cell.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Bacterial cells must first be made competent before they can be forced to take up plasmid DNA. Reason: DNA, being a hydrophilic molecule, cannot pass through cell membranes.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: DNA is hydrophilic and cannot pass through cell membranes on its own. Cells are therefore made competent, for example by calcium treatment and heat shock, to take up DNA. The Reason explains the Assertion.

options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I describes biolistics, not micro-injection, which injects rDNA directly into the nucleus of an animal cell. Statement II correctly describes heat shock.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. The origin of replication also controls the copy number of the linked DNA. II. Having more than one recognition site for an enzyme within a vector simplifies gene cloning. III. Normal Escherichia coli cells carry resistance against ampicillin. IV. In pBR322, alien DNA is ligated at a restriction site present in one of the two antibiotic resistance genes. Which of the above statements are correct?
explanation: Ori controls copy number, and in pBR322 foreign DNA goes into one resistance gene. Several sites for one enzyme generate several vector fragments and complicate cloning, and normal E. coli lacks resistance to ampicillin, which is why ampR works as a marker.

subject: Biology
question: After ligating foreign DNA at the BamH I site of pBR322 and transforming Escherichia coli, a colony grows on ampicillin medium. Which conclusion about this colony is valid?

options.A: It is an untransformed cell with natural ampicillin resistance
options.B: It is a transformant, but it may or may not be a recombinant
options.C: It is certainly a recombinant carrying the foreign DNA
options.D: It is certainly a non-recombinant with an empty plasmid

correct_answer: It is a transformant, but it may or may not be a recombinant
explanation: Both recombinant and non-recombinant plasmids keep ampR intact when the insert is at BamH I, so growth on ampicillin only shows transformation. Testing on tetracycline is needed: recombinants fail to grow there.

question: All of the following statements about vectors for plant and animal cells are correct EXCEPT:

options.A: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several dicot plants
options.B: the Ti plasmid has been modified into a vector that is no longer pathogenic to plants
options.C: retroviruses are used in their natural pathogenic form to deliver genes into animal cells
options.D: retroviruses have the ability to transform normal animal cells into cancerous cells

explanation: Retroviruses can transform normal cells into cancerous cells, so they are disarmed before use as vectors to deliver desirable genes into animal cells. The other statements are correct.

subject: Biology
question: A laboratory tries to run PCR using a DNA polymerase that is not thermostable, adding it only once at the beginning of the reaction. What is the expected outcome?

options.A: Primers fail to anneal because the template is degraded by the enzyme
options.B: Amplification is faster because the enzyme works best at high temperature
options.C: Amplification fails because the enzyme is inactivated at the high denaturation temperature

explanation: Denaturation uses high temperature. An ordinary polymerase is inactivated, so the primers are not extended in repeated cycles. Thermostable polymerase from Thermus aquaticus solves this.

question: A laboratory has cloned the gene for a therapeutic protein in Escherichia coli and optimised its expression, but cultures grown in small flasks give too little protein for clinical use. Which step will raise the yield of the protein?

question: Consider the following statements about population growth. I. Population density will increase if the number of births plus immigrants exceeds the number of deaths plus emigrants. II. subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. Population size is more technically called population density and is designated as N. II. Population density need not necessarily be measured in numbers only. III. Total number is an easily adoptable measure even when the population is huge and counting is very time-consuming. IV. Population density can sometimes be estimated indirectly, without actually counting or seeing the individuals. Which of the above are correct?
explanation: Population size, technically called population density (N), need not be measured in numbers only; per cent cover or biomass may be used. Total number is not easily adoptable when the population is huge and counting is impossible or very time-consuming. Population size can be estimated indirectly, without counting or seeing individuals, as in tiger census based on pug marks and fecal pellets.

question: Population size is not static. It keeps changing with time, depending on factors such as

options.B: pug marks, fecal pellets and number caught per trap
options.C: carrying capacity, biomass and relative density
options.D: food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather

correct_answer: food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather
explanation: Population density changes with time depending on food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather, acting through births, deaths, immigration and emigration.

List II: (I) Individuals of the population who left the habitat and went elsewhere during the period; (II) Number of births during a period added to the initial density; (III) Individuals of the same species that came into the habitat from elsewhere during the period; (IV) Number of deaths in the population during a given period. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Natality adds births, mortality removes deaths, immigration adds individuals of the same species coming from elsewhere, and emigration removes individuals leaving the habitat, each over the period under consideration.

question: A population has a density of 500 at time t. During the next unit of time there are 60 births, 20 immigrants, 40 deaths and 30 emigrants. Using Nt+1 = Nt + [(B + I) - (D + E)], what is the population density at time t + 1?

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: If a new habitat is just being colonised, immigration may contribute more significantly to population growth than birth rates. Reason: Under normal conditions, births and deaths are the most important factors influencing population density.

options.A: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Births and deaths dominate under normal conditions, whereas immigration and emigration assume importance only under special conditions such as colonisation of a new habitat. The reason describes the normal case and does not explain the special case.

subject: Biology
question: A bird population of 100 individuals is colonising a newly formed island. In one year it records 30 births, 50 immigrants, 20 deaths and 10 emigrants. Which conclusion is correct?

options.A: Density rises to 150, and immigration contributed more than births
options.B: Density rises to 180, and immigration contributed more than births
options.C: Density rises to 150, and births contributed more than immigration
options.D: Density rises to 110, since only births and deaths are counted

correct_answer: Density rises to 150, and immigration contributed more than births
explanation: Nt+1 = 100 + [(30 + 50) - (20 + 10)] = 150. In a newly colonised habitat immigration (50) contributed more to growth than births (30), as expected under such special conditions.

question: In a population of 5000 individuals, the per capita birth rate (b) is 0.05 and the per capita death rate (d) is 0.03 per year. Using dN/dt = (b - d) x N, what is the rate of change of population size?
explanation: r = b - d = 0.05 - 0.03 = 0.02; dN/dt = 0.02 x 5000 = 100 individuals per year.

subject: Biology
question: A population with N0 = 1000 grows exponentially with r = 0.0693 per year. Using Nt = N0 e^rt, what is the population after 10 years? (Take e^0.693 = 2.)
explanation: rt = 0.0693 x 10 = 0.693, so Nt = 1000 x e^0.693 = 1000 x 2 = 2000. Exponential growth compounds, unlike simple linear addition.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: The intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) is a very important parameter for assessing the impacts of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth. Reason: In 1981, the r value for the human population in India was 0.0205.

options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true. r is important because it summarises the net per capita growth, allowing comparison of factors affecting growth. The 1981 Indian value is merely an example of r and does not explain its importance.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: The logistic growth model is considered a more realistic model than the exponential model. Reason: Resources for growth for most animal populations are finite and become limiting sooner or later.

options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Since resources for most animal populations are finite and become limiting sooner or later, growth slows and levels off at K, as the logistic model describes. The reason explains the assertion.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: A population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote. Reason: In logistic growth, the growth rate keeps increasing even after population density reaches the carrying capacity.

options.A: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Logistic growth passes through lag, acceleration, deceleration and an asymptote at K. At carrying capacity no further growth is possible, so the reason is false.

subject: Biology
question: Arrange the phases of growth of a population in a habitat with limited resources in the correct order. P. Acceleration phase; Q. Asymptote at carrying capacity; R. Lag phase; S. Deceleration phase.
explanation: A population with limited resources shows a lag phase, then acceleration, then deceleration and finally an asymptote when density reaches carrying capacity, producing a sigmoid curve.

subject: Biology
question: A population growing logistically has r = 0.1, K = 1000 and a current size N = 200. Using dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K), what is its current growth rate?
explanation: dN/dt = 0.1 x 200 x (800/1000) = 20 x 0.8 = 16 individuals per unit time.

subject: Biology
question: Four populations of a species grow logistically with the same r and K = 1000, but are currently of different sizes. Using dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K), which size gives the greatest absolute growth rate?
explanation: dN/dt is proportional to N(K - N): 200 x 800 = 160000; 500 x 500 = 250000; 800 x 200 = 160000; 950 x 50 = 47500. The rate is greatest at N = 500.

question: The sigmoid growth of a population in a habitat with limited resources, described by dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K), is called
explanation: A plot of N against time under limited resources is sigmoid; this is Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth, dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K).

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: In the logistic equation, when N equals K, dN/dt becomes zero. Statement II: In the logistic equation, the term (K - N)/K approaches 1 as N approaches K.

options.A: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.B: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: When N = K, (K - N)/K = 0, so dN/dt = 0 and growth stops at the asymptote. As N approaches K the term approaches 0, not 1; it is close to 1 only when N is very small.

subject: Biology
question: A logistically growing population is very small compared with its carrying capacity (N much less than K). How does its growth behave at this stage?

options.A: It is near zero, as the population is still far below K
options.B: It equals rK, independent of the present population size N
options.C: It approximates exponential growth, as (K - N)/K is close to 1
options.D: It is negative, since N lies far below the carrying capacity

correct_answer: It approximates exponential growth, as (K - N)/K is close to 1
explanation: When N is much less than K, (K - N)/K is nearly 1, so dN/dt is nearly rN, the exponential form. Resistance to growth becomes important only as N approaches K.

subject: Biology
question: Since no population in nature has unlimited resources at its disposal, limited resources lead to

options.A: competition among individuals, with the fittest surviving and reproducing
options.B: immediate extinction of the population in that habitat
options.C: cooperation among individuals, with all members surviving equally
options.D: unlimited J-shaped growth until the habitat becomes empty

correct_answer: competition among individuals, with the fittest surviving and reproducing
explanation: Limited resources lead to competition between individuals; eventually the fittest individual survives and reproduces. Many governments have likewise introduced restraints to limit human population growth.

subject: Biology
question: A graph of population density (N) against time (t) shows curve a rising ever more steeply, and curve b rising and then flattening near a horizontal dashed line. Which interpretation is correct?

options.A: Curve a is logistic with limited resources; the dashed line is r
options.B: Curve a is exponential with unlimited resources; the dashed line is K
options.C: Curve b is exponential with unlimited resources; the dashed line is K
options.D: Curve b is logistic; the dashed line is N0, the initial density

correct_answer: Curve a is exponential with unlimited resources; the dashed line is K
explanation: When resources do not limit growth, the plot is exponential (J-shaped, curve a). When resources limit growth, the plot is logistic (sigmoid, curve b) and levels off at the carrying capacity K, shown as the dashed line.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. In exponential growth, the change in N during unit time is given by dN/dt = (b - d) x N. II. In the exponential equation, b and d are the total numbers of births and deaths in the population. III. Nt = N0 e^rt is the integral form of the exponential growth equation. IV. The logistic growth equation is dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K). Which of the above are correct?
explanation: In dN/dt = (b - d) x N, b and d are per capita (not total) birth and death rates, and (b - d) = r. Nt = N0 e^rt is the integral form; the logistic equation includes the factor (K - N)/K.

question: In the equation dN/dt = rN, the intrinsic rate of natural increase r is

options.D: per capita birth rate divided by per capita death rate

correct_answer: per capita birth rate minus per capita death rate
explanation: If b and d are per capita birth and death rates, then dN/dt = (b - d) x N; setting (b - d) = r gives dN/dt = rN.

subject: Biology
question: Populations evolve to maximise their reproductive fitness in the habitat in which they live. This fitness is also called

options.B: Carrying fitness, reflected in a high K value

options.D: Darwinian fitness, reflected in a low r value

correct_answer: Darwinian fitness, reflected in a high r value
explanation: Populations evolve to maximise reproductive fitness, also called Darwinian fitness (high r value), in their habitat. Under particular selection pressures, organisms evolve towards the most efficient reproductive strategy.

question: Even a plant species, which makes its own food, cannot survive alone in a natural habitat because it

options.C: needs other plants of its own species to fix atmospheric carbon for it

question: Match List I with List II, where + is beneficial, - is detrimental and 0 is neutral for species A and B respectively. List I: (P) Commensalism; (Q) Amensalism; (R) Competition; (S) Mutualism. List II: (I) +, +; (II) -, -; (III) +, 0; (IV) -, 0. Choose the correct option.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. In amensalism, one species is harmed whereas the other is unaffected. II. In both parasitism and predation, only one species benefits and the interaction is detrimental to the other. III. In commensalism, one species benefits while the other is slightly harmed. IV. Interspecific interactions arise from the interaction of populations of two different species. Which of the above are correct?
explanation: Amensalism is (-, 0); predation and parasitism are (+, -); commensalism is (+, 0), so the second species is unaffected, not harmed. Interspecific interactions involve populations of two different species.

options.D: Both species benefit from the interaction

correct_answer: Only one species benefits and the interaction harms the other
explanation: In both predation and parasitism only one species benefits (predator or parasite) and the interaction is detrimental to the other (prey or host); both are (+, -).

question: Predation can be thought of as nature's way of

subject: Biology
question: In a field experiment in the rocky intertidal communities of the American Pacific Coast, all the starfish Pisaster were removed from an enclosed area, and more than 10 species of invertebrates became extinct within a year. What does this best demonstrate?

options.A: Prey species become extinct mainly due to overexploitation by predators
options.B: Predators maintain species diversity by reducing competition among prey species
options.C: Invertebrates depend on Pisaster as a mutualist for food supply
options.D: Predators reduce species diversity by eliminating their preferred prey species

correct_answer: Predators maintain species diversity by reducing competition among prey species
explanation: After Pisaster was removed, more than 10 invertebrate species became extinct within a year because of interspecific competition. Predators help maintain species diversity in a community by reducing the intensity of competition among competing prey species.

question: Assertion: Predators in nature are said to be prudent. Reason: If a predator is too efficient and overexploits its prey, the prey might become extinct and, following it, the predator will also become extinct for lack of food.

options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Overexploitation of prey could drive the prey and then the predator itself to extinction. This is the reason why predators in nature are prudent, so the reason explains the assertion.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: Resources must always be limiting for competition to occur between two species. Statement II: In interference competition, the feeding efficiency of one species might be reduced by the interfering and inhibitory presence of the other species, even if resources are abundant.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Resources need not be limiting for competition to occur; in interference competition one species reduces the feeding efficiency of the other even when food and space are abundant. So statement I is incorrect and statement II is correct.

subject: Biology
question: Competition is best defined as a process in which

options.A: two closely related species always share a limiting resource and both become extinct
options.B: one species kills and eats another species occupying the same habitat
options.C: the fitness of one species (its r) is significantly lower in the presence of another
options.D: one species is harmed while the presence of the other remains entirely unaffected

correct_answer: the fitness of one species (its r) is significantly lower in the presence of another
explanation: Since unrelated species can compete and resources need not be limiting, competition is best defined as a process in which the fitness of one species (measured by r, the intrinsic rate of increase) is significantly lower in the presence of another species.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. According to Gause, two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot co-exist indefinitely and the competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually. II. Evidence for competitive exclusion occurring in nature is always conclusive. III. More recent studies suggest that species facing competition might evolve mechanisms that promote co-existence rather than exclusion. IV. Two competing species could avoid competition by choosing different times for feeding or different foraging patterns. Which of the above are correct?
explanation: Gause's principle states that the inferior competitor is eventually eliminated, but evidence in nature is not always conclusive. Recent studies show that competing species may evolve co-existence mechanisms, such as resource partitioning through different feeding times or foraging patterns.

subject: Biology
question: Many parasites have evolved to be host-specific. As a result, host and parasite tend to

options.D: co-evolve, each countering the other's mechanisms

explanation: Host-specific parasites and their hosts co-evolve: if the host evolves mechanisms to reject or resist the parasite, the parasite must evolve mechanisms to counteract and neutralise them to succeed with the same host species.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements about commensalism. I. An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch benefits, while the mango tree derives no apparent benefit. II. The sea anemone does not appear to derive any benefit by hosting the clown fish. Which of the above are correct?
explanation: In commensalism one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited: epiphytic orchid on mango, barnacles on a whale, cattle egret with grazing cattle, and clown fish with sea anemone. The whale and the anemone derive no apparent benefit.

question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Lichen; (Q) Mycorrhiza; (R) Fig tree; (S) Ophrys. subject: Biology
question: In mycorrhizae, the benefit exchanged between the two partners is that

options.A: the plant absorbs nutrients for the fungi, and the fungi supply carbohydrates
options.B: the fungi fix light energy, and the plant supplies water and minerals
options.C: the fungi protect the root from predators, and the plant supplies nectar
options.D: the fungi help in absorbing nutrients, and the plant supplies carbohydrates

correct_answer: the fungi help in absorbing nutrients, and the plant supplies carbohydrates
explanation: In mycorrhizae, associations between fungi and roots of higher plants, the fungi help the plant absorb essential nutrients from the soil while the plant provides the fungi with energy-yielding carbohydrates.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: Plants offer juicy and nutritious fruits as rewards to their seed dispersers. Reason: The female fig wasp uses the developing seeds within the fig fruit for nourishing its larvae.

options.A: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.C: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Plants pay fees to animals: pollen and nectar for pollinators and juicy, nutritious fruits for seed dispersers. The fig wasp feeding its larvae on developing seeds is a separate pollination mutualism and does not explain why fruits reward seed dispersers.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: In many species of fig trees, a given fig species can be pollinated only by its partner wasp species and no other species. Statement II: The female wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg-laying sites in the fruit.

options.A: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Many fig species have a tight one-to-one relationship with their pollinator wasp. The female wasp uses the fruit as an oviposition site and pollinates the inflorescence while searching for egg-laying sites; in return the fig offers some developing seeds as food for wasp larvae.

subject: Biology
question: Assertion: If the colour patterns of the female bee change even slightly during evolution, pollination success of Ophrys will be reduced unless the orchid flower co-evolves. Reason: Ophrys depends on one petal bearing an uncanny resemblance to the female of the bee in size, colour and markings to attract the male bee.

options.B: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
options.C: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.D: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Ophrys relies on sexual deceit: a petal mimics the female bee. If the female bee's patterns change, the mimicry fails and pollination success falls unless the orchid co-evolves. The reason explains the assertion and shows co-evolution at work.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. Plants offer pollen and nectar as rewards to their pollinators. II. The mutually beneficial system must be safeguarded against cheaters, such as animals that steal nectar without aiding pollination. III. All orchids offer rewards to their pollinators. IV. Many orchid floral patterns have evolved to attract the right pollinator insect, such as bees and bumblebees. Which of the above are correct?

subject: Biology
question: Many ecologists regard the entire biosphere as

options.A: A community of organisms that excludes the abiotic environment
options.B: A global ecosystem that is a composite of all local ecosystems on Earth
options.C: A single population of interbreeding organisms spread over the Earth
options.D: A single biome restricted to the land surfaces and freshwaters of the Earth

correct_answer: A global ecosystem that is a composite of all local ecosystems on Earth
explanation: The biosphere is regarded as a global ecosystem, a composite of all the local ecosystems on Earth. Because it is too big and complex to study as one unit, it is divided into terrestrial and aquatic categories.

question: Match List I with List II for a pond ecosystem. List I: (P) Abiotic component; (Q) Autotrophic component; (R) Consumers; (S) Decomposers. List II: (I) Zooplankton, free swimming and bottom dwelling forms; (II) Fungi, bacteria and flagellates; (III) Water with dissolved substances and bottom soil deposit; (IV) Phytoplankton, some algae and marginal plants. Choose the correct option.
explanation: In a pond, the abiotic component is water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances and the rich soil deposit at the bottom. Autotrophs are phytoplankton, some algae and floating, submerged and marginal plants. Consumers are zooplankton and free swimming and bottom dwelling forms. Decomposers are fungi, bacteria and flagellates.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following events that occur in a pond ecosystem. I. Conversion of inorganic into organic material by autotrophs using radiant energy of the sun. II. Consumption of the autotrophs by heterotrophs. III. Decomposition and mineralisation of dead organic matter to release it for reuse by autotrophs. IV. Cyclic return of energy from higher trophic levels to the autotrophs. Which of these events occur?
explanation: A pond converts inorganic into organic material using solar energy, heterotrophs consume autotrophs, and dead organic matter is decomposed and mineralised for reuse by autotrophs. Energy moves unidirectionally towards higher trophic levels and is dissipated as heat; it does not return to autotrophs.

subject: Biology
question: In a pond, which of the following is released back by decomposition for reuse by the autotrophs?

options.A: Heat energy lost during respiration of consumers
options.B: Inorganic nutrients from dead organic matter
options.C: Radiant energy stored earlier by phytoplankton
options.D: Organic matter of living zooplankton bodies

correct_answer: Inorganic nutrients from dead organic matter
explanation: Decomposition and mineralisation of dead organic matter release inorganic nutrients that are reused by autotrophs. Energy, in contrast, flows in one direction and is lost as heat, so it is not reused.

explanation: An ecosystem comprises abiotic and biotic components. Abiotic components are inorganic materials such as air, water and soil, whereas biotic components are producers, consumers and decomposers.

subject: Biology
question: Primary production is defined as the

options.A: Amount of organic matter left per unit area over a time period after decomposition
options.B: Amount of new organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by consumers
options.C: Amount of solar energy falling per unit area over a time period on the plant canopy layer
options.D: Amount of biomass produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis

correct_answer: Amount of biomass produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis
explanation: Primary production is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed as weight (g m^-2) or energy (kcal m^-2).

subject: Biology
question: To compare the productivity of different ecosystems, productivity is expressed in terms of

options.A: g m^-3 yr^-1 or kcal m^-3 only
options.B: g yr^-1 or kcal yr^-1 only
options.C: g m^-2 or kcal m^-2 only
options.D: g m^-2 yr^-1 or kcal m^-2 yr^-1

correct_answer: g m^-2 yr^-1 or kcal m^-2 yr^-1
explanation: Productivity is the rate of biomass production and is expressed as g m^-2 yr^-1 or kcal m^-2 yr^-1 so that ecosystems can be compared. Production itself, without the time rate, is expressed as g m^-2 or kcal m^-2.

subject: Biology
question: In a forest, producers use 40 per cent of the gross primary productivity in respiration, and the net primary productivity is 1200 g m^-2 yr^-1. What is the gross primary productivity?
explanation: If respiration is 40 per cent of GPP, NPP is 60 per cent of GPP. So GPP = 1200 / 0.6 = 2000 g m^-2 yr^-1. Respiration is 800 and 2000 - 800 = 1200.

question: Net primary productivity represents the biomass that is available for consumption by

options.C: Carnivores alone, through predation on herbivores

explanation: GPP minus respiration losses is NPP, and NPP is the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs, that is, herbivores and decomposers.

question: Two ecosystems have exactly the same standing crop of producers on a given day. Which conclusion is valid?

question: Assertion: Ecosystems need a constant supply of energy to synthesise the molecules they require. Reason: Energy captured by producers is returned to them by decomposers and reused.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements about why tropics show greater biological diversity. I. Temperate regions were subjected to frequent glaciations, while tropical latitudes remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years. II. Tropical environments are more seasonal than temperate environments. III. More solar energy is available in the tropics, contributing to higher productivity. IV. Tropical environments are less constant and less predictable than temperate ones. Which of these statements are correct?
explanation: The hypotheses are: tropics had long undisturbed evolutionary time while temperate regions suffered glaciations; tropical environments are less seasonal, more constant and predictable, promoting niche specialisation; and more solar energy in the tropics raises productivity, which might indirectly support more diversity.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: Humboldt observed that within a region species richness increases with explored area without any limit. Statement II: On a logarithmic scale, the species-area relationship is a straight line.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. Z, the slope of the log species-area line, is also called the regression coefficient. II. On ordinary axes, the species-area relationship for many taxa is a rectangular hyperbola. III. For very large areas like entire continents, the slope is shallower than for smaller regions. IV. Humboldt observed that species richness increases with explored area only up to a limit. Which of these statements are correct?
explanation: Z is the slope (regression coefficient), the relationship is a rectangular hyperbola on ordinary axes, and Humboldt noted an increase only up to a limit. For entire continents the slope is steeper (Z 0.6 to 1.2), not shallower.

explanation: S2/S1 = (A2/A1)^Z = 32^0.2. Since 32 = 2^5, 32^0.2 = 2^1 = 2. Species richness doubles.

question_type: Match List I and List II
question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Narrowly utilitarian; (Q) Broadly utilitarian; (R) Ethical; (S) Bioprospecting. List II: (I) Ecosystem services such as oxygen production and pollination; (II) Direct economic benefits such as food, firewood and fibre; (III) Exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for economically important products; (IV) Every species has an intrinsic value. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Narrowly utilitarian reasons are direct benefits like food, firewood, fibre and medicines; broadly utilitarian reasons are ecosystem services like oxygen production and pollination; the ethical argument is that every species has intrinsic value; bioprospecting explores diversity for economically important products.

subject: Biology
question: Statement I: Industrial products such as tannins, lubricants, dyes, resins and perfumes are direct benefits under the narrowly utilitarian argument. Statement II: Pollination by bees, bumblebees, birds and bats is classified under the ethical argument.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Industrial products are direct economic benefits, so they are narrowly utilitarian. Pollination is an ecosystem service, so it is broadly utilitarian, not ethical.

subject: Biology
question: Consider the following statements. I. More than 25 percent of the drugs currently sold in the market worldwide are derived from plants. II. About 2,500 species of plants contribute to the medicines of native peoples around the world. III. Bioprospecting is exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance. IV. Pollination is a narrowly utilitarian benefit. Which of these statements are correct?
explanation: More than 25 percent of drugs sold worldwide are derived from plants, and 25,000 species of plants (not 2,500) contribute to the medicines of native peoples. Bioprospecting explores diversity for economically important products. Pollination is broadly utilitarian.

question: Assertion: Species that have no current economic value should also be conserved. Reason: Every species has an intrinsic value, and we have a moral duty to care for its well-being and pass on our biological legacy in good order to future generations.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
options.B: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
options.C: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
options.D: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The ethical argument holds that we share the planet with millions of species, each with intrinsic value even if not of current economic value, and we have a moral duty to care for them and pass on our biological legacy to future generations.

question: Assertion: Sacred groves are an ex situ strategy of biodiversity conservation. Reason: In sacred groves, all the trees and wildlife are venerated and given total protection.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following are ex situ conservation approaches? I. Fertilising eggs of threatened species in vitro after cryopreservation of gametes. II. Propagating plants using tissue culture methods. III. Protecting species within biosphere reserves. IV. Maintaining animals in wildlife safari parks.
explanation: Ex situ approaches include zoological parks, botanical gardens and wildlife safari parks, cryopreservation of gametes with in vitro fertilisation, tissue culture propagation and seed banks. Biosphere reserves protect species in their natural habitat, which is in situ.

question: Assertion: Seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants can be kept for long periods in seed banks. Reason: Gametes of threatened species can be preserved in viable and fertile condition for long periods using cryopreservation.

explanation: Both are ex situ techniques: seed banks store seeds of commercially important plant strains, and cryopreservation keeps gametes viable and fertile for long periods. They are parallel methods; one does not explain the other.

subject: Biology
subtopic: In situ and ex situ conservation
question: Consider the following statements. I. The three hotspots covering India are the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Himalaya. II. In Meghalaya, sacred groves are the last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants. III. Many animals that have become extinct in the wild continue to be maintained in zoological parks. IV. Saving the entire forest to save the tiger is an example of ex situ conservation. Which of these statements are correct?
explanation: India's three hotspots are the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Himalaya; Meghalaya's sacred groves are last refuges for many rare plants; zoos maintain many animals extinct in the wild. Saving the entire forest to save the tiger protects the whole ecosystem on site, which is in situ conservation.

question: Match List I with List II. List I: (P) Convention on Biological Diversity (The Earth Summit); (Q) World Summit on Sustainable Development; (R) Year by which a significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity loss was pledged; (S) Number of countries that made this pledge. List II: (I) 190; (II) Johannesburg, 2002; (III) 2010; (IV) Rio de Janeiro, 1992. Choose the correct option.
explanation: The Earth Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992. As a follow-up, the World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg in 2002 saw 190 countries pledge to achieve a significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity loss by 2010. Since biodiversity knows no political boundaries, its conservation is a collective responsibility of all nations.
